brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Two columns of half-n bases, each three high (piece:0,0,0..2 and piece:1,0,0..2), joined by snaps and bolted.
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut, on the cut faces of the two level-0 half bases.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-half-n-full-div2 and bin:1,0,2~hex-bin-half-n-full-div2, with nothing on top, so they stay open.

finish.summary: I built a three-storey tower that's two columns wide. It's made of North-half hex bases stacked three high at cells (0,0) and (1,0), at levels 0 to 2. I removed the full base that was on the screen at the start, because a drawer only fits on the cut face of a half base, and a half base can only carry another half of the same kind on top of it. The bottom storey has two drawers on the south cut face, one per column. The top storey has two open bins, each full depth and split in two. Nothing is on top of the bins. I then ran the house rules: open edges are closed with solid end caps and the joints are bolted. The check found no rule errors and the collision check came back clear. The middle storey's front cut faces are still open, with no drawer or bin. The build is 49 parts, a bit over the usual 40, because of the second column and its caps. I didn't add any props, since the brief is about the structure.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
